content.intro: Learn modern model field fetching through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Modern Model Field Fetching matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines modern model field fetching as part of the django orm and querysets. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Understanding deferred and unfetched fields; Explicit versus on-demand data fetching; Django 6.1 model field fetch modes; Measuring the trade-offs of field-fetching strategies; Compatibility considerations when upgrading older models. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

content_blocks.title: Version note: Django 6.1
content_blocks.text: Fetch modes are new in Django 6.1. The example uses `QuerySet.fetch_mode(models.FETCH_PEERS)`; confirm the installed patch release and official fetch-mode documentation before adopting it. This does not remove the need to benchmark traditional `select_related()` / `prefetch_related()` strategies.

items.title: Django 6.1 model field fetch modes
items.text: Django 6.1 introduced model field fetch modes. `FETCH_ONE`, `FETCH_PEERS`, and `FETCH_RAISE` affect on-demand fetching; check the version-specific docs and compare with traditional eager-loading methods.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Modern Model Field Fetching
content_blocks.code:
from django.db import models

books = Book.objects.fetch_mode(models.FETCH_PEERS)
for book in books:
    print(book.author.name)
content_blocks.expected_output: On Django 6.1, FETCH_PEERS can fetch an unfetched field for peer instances from a QuerySet and reduce common repeated field-fetch queries.
